question.text: Identify the correct statement from the following in a chemical reaction.

options.text: The change in entropy along with suitable change in enthalpy decides the rate of reaction
Both the enthalpy and the entropy remain constant

solution.text:
\(\Delta \mathrm{G}(\mathrm{T}, \mathrm{P})=\Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}\) gives the free energy of system.
When \(\Delta \mathrm{G}(\mathrm{T}, \mathrm{P})<0\), the reaction is spontaneous.
When \(\Delta \mathrm{G}(\mathrm{T}, \mathrm{P})>0\), the reaction is non-spontaneous.
Hence, entropy changed with a suitable change in enthalpy will decide the rate of the reaction.
